checks.label: As Q gets closer to P, the slope of the chord becomes a better approximation to the rate of change at P: on the boat at P, from either side, each shorter chord the page uses is nearer the rate there than the one before, and at every stop of the slider the chord drawn, the working and the table give the slope the rule gives, with the amount above the rate equal to the gap

Recognize a tangent to a curve at a point as the limit of secant lines: every tangent the page draws goes through its point P with the slope the chords there settle on from either side, and read back through the axes its drawn gradient is that slope

Discusses the meaning of the limiting value of δy/δx as δx shrinks towards nought, defining it as dy/dx: on the δ screen δy/δx reads the rule's chord slope at each gap it stops at, and dy/dx is the number those slopes settle on

From the rules: f(3) = 9 m and the chord from 3 s to 4 s is 16 − 9 = 7 m per s; chords from 3 s read 7, 6.5, 6.1, 6.01 and 6.001 m per s, each above 6 by its gap; chords ending at 3 s from 2, 2.9, 2.99 and 2.999 s read 5, 5.9, 5.99 and 5.999; f(3.5) = 12.25 m, 3.25 m above P, and 12.25 ÷ 3.5 = 3.5; f(2.9) = 8.41 m; f(3.001) = 9.006001 m; from 2 s the chords read 5, 4.1 and 4.01 and settle on 4, while 4 ÷ 2 = 2; the tank holds 50 L at 5 min, its chords read −19.8 and −19.98 and settle on −20 L per min; and the screens' sentences quote these same values

Every puzzle offers three different answers and accepts only the right one; each wrong answer is the slip it stands for: 3.5 m per s and 3.25 m against 6.5 m per s; 6 m per s and 0.006001 m against 6.001 m per s; 6.1 m per s and 0.59 m against 5.9 m per s; 9 m and 6.001 m per s against 6 m per s; 3 m per s and 0 ÷ 0, no answer against 6 m per s; −19.98 L per min and 50 L against −20 L per min; 5 m per s and 2 m per s against 4 m per s
Before an answer no puzzle shows it: no tangent, nothing red, and the working ends in a question mark; a right answer shows its value with nothing red, and every wrong answer shows its slip in red
Every chord is drawn as a straight line through P and Q, and its gradient read back through the axes is the slope in the working
Dragging Q keeps it on a half second inside the axes and never on P, so every chord it makes has a gap
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 1.3 s
